title: 11wdrg4
The Bay'a and the Camel
hook: When the people ran to Imam Ali, he took up the heavy caliphate knowingly. His resolve for justice gave birth to the Camel.
scenes.0.text: After the beatification, **Ali** immediately went to work. The order that he overthrew had been broken for years. There was favoritism, unjustly distributed property, and oppressive governors. Ali first returned the property unjustly given to the beytullah, the common treasury of the ummah. Then he removed the governors who had been criticized by the people. These decisions disturbed those who had gained wealth and power during the Ottoman era. Ali's justice soon produced enemies who would draw swords against him. First in Basra, then in Siffin, the price of that justice would be paid.
scenes.0.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.1.text: **Talha** and Zubair had also made a vow to **Ali** in Medina. But it became a promise on their lips, not in their hearts. Both of them sought a high position in the state from Ali and looked to the governorships of Basra and Kufa. Ali refused this request because he didn't think it was right to be biased. When Uthman changed governors, he didn't give them what they expected. He returned the wronged property to the house and did not favor anyone. In Damascus, the deputy governor refused to give up his seat. The loss of offices and the confiscation of property was the main cause of the objection. But the protesters have cited Uthman's blood as a reason. Uthman's blood has become an excuse for anyone whose interests have been harmed.
scenes.1.art.actors.0.label: s20l3t
Talha
scenes.1.art.actors.1.label: 52j0kp
Al-Zubayr
scenes.1.art.actors.2.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.2.text: The governor of Damascus, Mu'awiya, announced that he would not beatify **Ali** until Uthman's killers were punished. Uthman's blood was a motive for him. What he wanted was to maintain his power and reach for power. Ali wanted to restore order first and then see justice done. He knew that a hasty revenge would cause another mess. First he wrote letters, then he sent envoys. He always saw the sword as a last resort.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: 1inzbgl
Mu'awiya
scenes.3.text: Meanwhile, he met Aisha, Talha and Zubair, who were in Mecca for Umrah. Talha and Zubair, unable to obtain their desired position, set off with Aisha towards Basra, using Uthman's blood as an excuse. They gathered an army against **Ali**, whom they had bequeathed. So they reopened the newly adopted caliphate to debate. It wasn't the banner at Ghadir on the road to Basra that was mentioned, but the blood of Uthman. Almost a quarter of a century after the Prophet's death, the Muslims were being drawn into a major war among themselves for the first time.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: rrckkf
Aisha
scenes.3.art.actors.1.label: s20l3t
Talha
scenes.3.art.actors.2.label: 52j0kp
Al-Zubayr
scenes.4.text: The army marched from Mecca to Basra one night and came to a body of water called Ha'ab. The dogs started barking in the dark. Aisha asked, "What kind of water is this?" They said, "Hawa'ib". Aisha suddenly stopped, because she remembered a saying of the Prophet to his wives: "What will happen to you when the dogs of Ha'av bark for one of you?" He wanted to come back right away. But Talha and Zubair's companions convinced him to continue. According to the people of Bethlehem, false witnesses were brought and they were made to swear, "This is not Ha'abeeb". When the army reached Basra, clashes broke out with Ali's governor Uthman b. Huneyf, and the first bloodshed took place there.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: rrckkf
Aisha
scenes.5.text: **Ali** marched to Basra with his army. He repeatedly sent envoys to prevent war. When the two armies came face to face, he called Zubair to his ranks and reminded him of a day many years ago. When the Prophet saw them together, he said to Zubair, "Do you love him?" Zubair said, "Yes, why shouldn't I love him?" The Prophet said, "But one day you will oppose him and fight him unjustly". When Zubair heard this, he bowed his head and said, "I forgot". He said he wasn't going to fight, turned around and left the battlefield. But after he left, he was killed on the way.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.5.art.actors.1.label: 52j0kp
Al-Zubayr
scenes.6.text: When all attempts at peace failed, the two armies clashed. In the middle of the battle was the camel that Aisha was riding. The soldiers of the other side were gathering around the camel. As long as the camel stood, the battle was on. Ali ordered the camel to be slaughtered to stop the bloodshed. Around the camel, about seventy of the men guarding the back of the camel died. And when the she-camel fell down, she could not find a place to gather, and the army was scattered. **Talha** was killed in this battle. This battle is called the Camel War, after the camel.
scenes.6.art.actors.1.label: rrckkf
Aisha
scenes.6.art.actors.2.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.7.text: By the time the war was over, **Ali** had won, but he never enjoyed any victory. He freed the prisoners. He made no provision for the spoils of the defeated party, nor for his wives and children. He wouldn't let anyone break into his house or take anything he owned. He respected Aisha as the wife of the Prophet. He dismissed him to Medina with honour, alongside his brother Muhammad b. Abi Bekir. Ali, who was fair even to those who drew his sword, upheld the Prophet's morality even in the middle of the battlefield.
scenes.7.art.actors.0.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.7.art.actors.1.label: rrckkf
Aisha
scenes.7.art.actors.2.label: yenjdy
Muhammad b. Abi Bakr
scenes.8.text: Aisha felt deep regret for participating in this war after Jamal. Ali, on the other hand, was both patient and truthful against those who broke his promise. That bloody day in Basra was over, but a greater test lay ahead for Ali. In Damascus, Mu'awiya was still recovering and was gathering a large army on the pretext of Uthman's blood. After Basra, Ali moved to Kufa and made it the center of his caliphate. Soon he would face Mu'awiya's army at the Euphrates at Siphin.
scenes.8.art.actors.0.label: rrckkf
Aisha
sunni.0.says: The bay'a to Imam Ali, Mu'awiya's stance, the setting out for Basra, the Battle of the Camel and its aftermath; the report of the reminder to al-Zubayr is also transmitted.
sunni.1.says: The account of how the bay'a was taken and of the process leading to the Camel.
sunni.2.says: The course of the Battle of the Camel.
sunni.3.says: Reports about Aisha and the events; reports narrating that Aisha regretted are transmitted in this source and in works such as Ibn Abi Shayba, al-Dhahabi and al-Hakim.
sunni.4.says: Aisha reaches the waters of Banu Amir at night. Dogs bark. She asks the name of the water. When told Haw'ab, she wants to turn back. Those with her, al-Zubayr among them, tell her to go on. She remembers the Prophet's saying, "How will it be with you when the dogs of Haw'ab bark at one of you?"
sunni.4.grade: The text was read in the Musnad under these numbers
sunni.5.says: No. 5573: Imam Ali reminds al-Zubayr that, while they were together in the shade of one of the Ansar, the Prophet asked "Do you love him?", that al-Zubayr said yes, and that he said, "You will oppose him and fight him, wronging him." Al-Zubayr turns back. No. 5574: "You will fight him and you will be the one who wrongs him." Al-Zubayr says he had forgotten and leaves. Al-Hakim says this report is sahih. No. 5575: Al-Zubayr tells the hadith to his son Abdullah and leaves, breaking through the ranks.
sunni.6.says: He says that Ali was right about Jamal; Talha, Zubeir and Aisha are wrong.
sunni.7.says: The view that Ali was right in Jemel and the other side was wrong is attributed to him; the rules of war with the rebels are removed from Ali's Jemel practice.
sunni.8.says: The war against the rebels (not to kill the wounded, not to pursue the fugitive, not to count the property as booty) is derived from the behavior of Hz. Ali in Jemel and Siffin.
shia.0.says: Imam Ali's conditions for accepting the caliphate and his sermon upon the insistence on the bay'a. There is debate over the attribution of the sermons.
shia.1.says: Aisha's desire to return to Ha'abe, false witnesses saying "This is not Ha'abe" and Zubair being reminded of the Prophet's words and his leaving the battlefield.
shia.2.says: The first correspondence between Imam Ali and Mu'awiya. In Sunni rijal criticism Nasr is counted as an "extreme Shia," but in terms of material he is an early source.
shia.3.says: The general course of events. He is considered a historian with Shia leanings.
disputes.0.title: uex6wm
Caliph Uthman's blood: order first, or retribution first?
disputes.0.sunni: Caliph Uthman's blood has been discussed on both sides. The Sunni view understands both Imam Ali's reasoning and the stance of the other side as an ijtihad.
disputes.0.shia: Caliph Uthman's blood has been discussed on both sides. In the Shia account, Imam Ali wanted first to establish order and leave the case to the judiciary, and opposition to this is not seen as legitimate.
disputes.1.title: az03t4
Was the bay'a of Talha and al-Zubayr from the heart?
disputes.1.sunni: That Talha and al-Zubayr pledged allegiance is common ground in the sources. Whether this bay'a was given voluntarily or under pressure is separately reported.
disputes.1.shia: That Talha and al-Zubayr pledged allegiance is common ground in the sources. Imam Ali maintained that this bay'a was given from the heart and did not accept the later claim that it was given under compulsion.
disputes.2.title: 1qoyfta
What was Aisha's grief about?
disputes.2.sunni: Reports narrating that Aisha was grieved are found in the sources. The chain of each report and the subject of the grief are separately debated.
disputes.2.shia: Reports narrating that Aisha was grieved are found in the sources. In the Shia account, her opposition to Imam Ali is seen as a wrong step.
questions.0: When Ali took over the caliphate, he took back the wrongful possessions and reduced the corrupt governors. How do you think these decisions have affected the attitude of those who opposed him in Cemal and Siffin?
questions.1: When Ali reminded Zubair of the Prophet's question, "Do you love him?" and the words, "You will fight against him by oppressing him", Zubair left the group. Why do you think this reminder led Zubair to leave the group?
questions.2: After the battle, Ali released the prisoners and respectfully dismissed Aisha to Medina. Why do you think Ali let the prisoners go when he was victorious?
questions.3: Many Sunni scholars find Ali closer to the truth in Jamal. Why do you think this shared view is so far beyond sectarianism?
summary: After the assassination of Caliph Uthman, Ali consciously assumed the caliphate. He wanted to return to Aisha in Ha'eb, but was persuaded to continue on the road. Ali reminded Zubair of the words of the Prophet. Zubair left the compound and was later killed. Ali pardoned the prisoners and respectfully dismissed Aisha to Medina.
key: The first civil war against Imam Ali
notes.0: After Caliph Uthman was killed, Imam Ali took up the caliphate knowingly.
notes.1: Talha, al-Zubayr and Aisha cited Caliph Uthman's blood as justification and turned toward Basra.
notes.2: Mu'awiya, too, announced that he would not pledge allegiance until Caliph Uthman's blood was avenged.
notes.3: At the Camel, when the Prophet's saying was recalled to him, al-Zubayr left the battlefield and was later killed. Talha was killed in the battle.
notes.4: After the battle, Imam Ali released the prisoners and sent Aisha off to Medina with respect.
